claims.quote: The sitting room in the cottage had the small, borrowed luxury of rooms that meant to be kind and not show it. A lamp with a soft, honeyed shade stood behind an armchair and found little pockets of warmth across the rug; a silk shawl—pale, not yet folded—lay over the back of the other chair as if someone had just paused in the act of leaving it. A low table was set between them with a book and a small bowl of shelled nuts; beyond, a narrow sideboard held a decanter, a pair of short glasses and a metal bucket of crushed ice, the sight of which tasted like improbability and courtesy in the heat of June.
claims.value: lamp; armchairs; silk shawl; low table; bowl of shelled nuts; sideboard with decanter; pair of short glasses; metal bucket of crushed ice

claims.quote: The paper waited on her lap in its single fold—three loose leaves, corners softened—edges thumbed, the margins pencilled with a few neat carets and one underlining at the bottom of the first page.
claims.value: three loose leaves; margins with pencil carets; one underlining on first page

claims.quote: The actress folded the script back into its flap, put it in the neat leather bag at her feet, and for a moment the two women sat with the same small, unsent things between them: the glass, the folded paper, the knowledge that some performances belonged to no audience.
claims.value: in leather bag at her feet

claims.quote: She did not drink for show. The gin and tonic was cold enough to make a faint sound when the ice settled; the glass gave away the summer in a smell of citrus peel and juniper.

The confidante hovered in the doorway and then drew up an easy chair as if to keep the map of herself visible but small. She folded the telegrams into a drawer, looked at the actress with an impatience that was almost fondness, and arranged a small slip of paper on the mantel with two neat orders: No calls; do not admit; bring a glass if wished.
claims.value: remained in sitting room; occasional small check-ins; arranged privacy instructions

claims.quote: "I told the cottagekeeper to keep us private," she said, in the flat, usable voice years of studio fights had practiced. "If anyone comes, he refuses them. I'll be in the hall. I won't be far."
claims.value: cottagekeeper instructed to refuse callers and keep guests private

claims.quote: "I'll leave you an hour," she said, quick as a small trade. "Then I'll come back and I'll want to hear the end."
claims.value: plans to leave for an hour then return

claims.quote: Outside, the lane made a dull, late-summer noise: a bicycle bell, a distant cart; nothing impeached the cottage's claim to being ordinary.
claims.value: bicycle bell and distant cart noises present in lane outside
